action.desc: weight-space blend of the champion with an evolution child (x3 = blend g003 0.6; x4 = 0.7 x3 + 0.3 evo_g004/14300)
action.hypothesis: children that fail alone keep useful changes; averaging weights keeps the champion's strengths

result.notes: x3_g003_60 then x4_g004_70 promoted; gene children g009-g017 all rejected

lesson: In the flat loop, blending the champion with a near-miss child was the only route to promotion; single gene changes rarely survive the no-regression gate.

action.desc: children silently inherited K4 defaults (kick clips in AMP data, style near the ball, RSI 10/10 %)

result.notes: goals and long-kick power lower than the v58 recipe

lesson: Make every default a switchable gene and record the parent's exact recipe; a default change confounds every child that inherits it.

action.desc: robot test of the benchmark-rejected g014 and the champion x4

result.notes: g014 missed the ball repeatedly; x4 kicked accurately but slowly

lesson: The benchmark ranking predicted the robot; keep rejecting children with regressions even if they look faster.

action.desc: style runs sty_range / sty_free: inside foot (curriculum 20->90 deg) + hop, bundled with K4 (kick clips in AMP, style near ball, RSI B-Human 0.15)

result.notes: inside foot learned (88 % of short kicks at 16150); long-kick 3D 6.99 -> 4.70 m/s; free choice hopped 97 % of long kicks and 94 % of passes

lesson: A rising target-angle curriculum (B-Human style) teaches the inside foot where a fixed 90 deg reward did not (1 %); do not bundle known-harmful defaults (K4) into a new experiment; free style choice collapses onto the most rewarded style (hop).

action.desc: sty_power: K4 off, t.hop_power_long 800, w.long_kick_power 4000, 1000 it.

result.notes: v1: first kick 3.34 s (x4 3.73, B-Human 4.49); goals +12-18 %; aim 92 %; long 5.72 m/s; short planted 44 %; late falls 1.8 %

lesson: Power recovered only partly after the style curriculum; inside-foot passes with a hop are the remaining safety issue.

context.deployment: sim effort limits knee 112, hip roll 76, hip pitch 68, hip yaw / ankle 38.3 (motor no-load ratings)

action.desc: hard leg torque clip at B-Human's 50/50/30/60/30/30 N·m (user)

result.notes: all earlier numbers were without the clip; baselines re-measured

lesson: Use loaded torque limits, not motor ratings; keep them in one table until measured on the robot.

action.desc: bisected the runswift-vs-ours accuracy gap (torque, feet, model, integrator, delay, I/O, ONNX, caps, joint-target clip)

result.notes: runner clips joint targets to Q_ABS_LIMITS; training did not. x4 7/36 -> 31/36 within 15 deg with the clip removed; our sim + clip 90/108 -> 31/108. sty_power robust to it (84 -> 82 %)

lesson: Benchmark the deployed action path: any runner transform (clip, filter) must be in training and in the benchmark, or the policy learns to depend on what deployment removes (x4 pressed hip roll 0.38 rad past its stop).
A policy that only works inside its training delay range is brittle; train and test delay ranges that include zero.

action.desc: found why x4 fell in 34/90 goal-grid approaches

result.notes: all falls with the ball 148-180 deg behind, 0.7-1.2 s in; training spawns the ball within +-23 deg ahead only; our sim: 4-10 m behind -> 53-59 % falls in 3 s; v1 hid it (falls counted only after 2 s, approach probe did not gate falls)

lesson: Cover every start the robot can meet (ball behind, far) in training, and count falls from t = 0 in every benchmark situation.

context.bench: v2 GPU (deployed path, fixed caps / perception / delay, CIs)

action.desc: benchmark v2 on x4, sty_power_17149, B-Human

result.notes: sty_power vs x4: v2 fitness +48 (loop goals 1.11/1.57 vs 0.74/1.29, kicks <= 20 deg 96/80 vs 80/67 %), but long 3D 3.6-3.7 vs 4.7-4.9 m/s and ball-behind falls 43-45 vs 23-34 %; B-Human kick-only precision 99 % <= 20 deg with perfect ball but falls 55-61 % from our walking starts (not its deployment)

lesson: Under the deployed path the inside-foot lineage is the better policy; its weak spots (power, ball-behind falls) are the next targets.
